title: U.S. House · Maryland's 7th District
area: Most of Baltimore City and part of Baltimore County.

context.text: Incumbent Kweisi Mfume defeated Mark Conway, Tashi Davis and Theo Gillespie in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. Scott Collier, a repeat candidate for this and other Maryland seats, ran unopposed in the Republican primary.

summary.text: Kweisi Mfume is the Democratic incumbent in Maryland's 7th Congressional District. He previously represented the district from 1987 to 1996 before leading the NAACP as its president.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Morgan State University and a master's degree in international studies from Johns Hopkins University.
Served on the Baltimore City Council from 1978 to 1986 and represented Maryland's 7th District in Congress from 1987 to 1996.
Served as president of the NAACP after leaving Congress, before winning a 2020 special election to return to the House.

priorities.text: Community involvement and public policy shaped by his decades in Baltimore civic life.

record.text: As a Baltimore City Council member, chaired the Committee on Health Policy and led efforts to divest city funds from the apartheid government of South Africa.
Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and House Committee on Foreign Affairs for the 2025-2026 term.

summary.text: Scott Collier is the Republican nominee for Maryland's 7th Congressional District. A media entrepreneur, he has run unsuccessfully for various Maryland offices in recent cycles.

background.text: Graduated from Dundalk High School in 1981; has worked as a structural steel painter, home improvement specialist and media entrepreneur running DundalkTV.
Has run for U.S. House in Maryland's 7th District in 2022 and 2024, for the 2nd District in 2020, and for Maryland State Senate District 6 in 2018.

priorities.text: Giving political power back to the people and working together on solutions.

researchNotes: Scott Collier has not reported federal campaign contributions in any of his prior runs and has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey for this or any recent race; his only stated priority comes from a 2018 candidate survey for a different office (Maryland State Senate). His research depth is marked minimal.
